issues.description: The solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute (and corresponding constructor parameters) in Animal and all subclasses, whereas the problem statement UML and description define Animal with only a 'name' attribute. This creates a structural mismatch: students following the UML would implement constructors that take only a name, but the solution code requires an extra age parameter and stores an age field. This inconsistency can confuse students about the required attributes and constructor signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the problem UML: remove the 'age' attribute from Animal and update constructors in Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat to accept only the 'name' parameter (and update calls accordingly). Alternatively, if the age attribute is intended, update the problem statement and UML to include the 'age' attribute and clarify that constructors must accept both name and age.

issues.description: The solution introduces an extra attribute 'age' in Animal and uses two-argument constructors (String name, int age) for Seal/Pig/Goat, while the problem statement's UML and the template's Main usage assume animals have only a name and use single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This API/attribute mismatch prevents a direct mapping from the problem/template example to the solution implementation and will confuse students when instantiating animals or implementing constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the APIs consistent: either remove the additional 'age' attribute from the solution's Animal class and provide single-argument constructors (String name) for Seal/Pig/Goat to match the problem UML and template Main usage, or update the problem statement and template Main examples to document and use the two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and the added 'age' attribute so all artifacts align.
